question: Will the US put boots on the ground in Iran before September?
resolution_criteria:
Resolution criteria:

This market will resolve to YES if, at any point before September 1, 2026, the United States deploys active-duty military ground forces ("boots on the ground") on sovereign Iranian territory (including mainland Iran and its sovereign islands, such as Kharg Island).

Otherwise, this market will resolve to NO.

Definitions & Clarifications:

"Boots on the ground": Defined as the physical presence of U.S. military personnel (including Army, Marines, or Special Operations Forces) on dry land within Iran's borders for combat, securing infrastructure, or other military operations.

Exclusions: The following events will not trigger a YES resolution:

Naval blockades, ship boardings, or maritime operations in the Persian Gulf or Strait of Hormuz that do not involve forces landing on Iranian territory.

Aerial operations, including manned or unmanned airstrikes.

U.S. aircrews or pilots entering Iranian territory solely due to their aircraft being shot down, or search-and-rescue teams deployed specifically to retrieve downed personnel.
research:
# US boots on the ground in Iran before September 1, 2026: research brief (as of 2026-08-19)

## 1. Resolution source
- The criteria give no URL or named data source. In practice the question will be settled by credible media or official US (CENTCOM or Pentagon) confirmation of US ground forces on Iranian land.
- 2026-08-19: I found no credible report of US ground forces on Iranian territory for combat, holding ground or securing infrastructure since the conflict began. Several key pages (Al Jazeera, Fox live blog, Wikipedia, Manifold) would not load, so this is based on search summaries.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet. The only confirmed US ground entry so far was a combat search-and-rescue mission, which the criteria specifically exclude.
- 2026-04-03 to 04-05: After an F-15E was shot down, US special operations forces (including SEAL Team 6) went into Iran and got into a firefight while recovering both crew members. This falls under the downed-aircrew exclusion. Polymarket's dispute panel did count it as US forces "entering" Iran for its own market. [Task & Purpose](https://taskandpurpose.com/news/f15-airman-rescue-iran-special-operations.md), [The Week](https://www.theweek.in/news/middle-east/2026/04/11/amid-us-iran-stalemate-dollar269-million-question-divides-polymarket-did-american-forces-enter-tehran.amp.html)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-08-19: Trump announced what he called the "most crushing economic operation ever" against Iran, an economic measure rather than a ground action. [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/8/19/trump-announces-most-crushing-economic-operation-ever-against-iran)
- 2026-08-17: The 60-day US-Iran memorandum of understanding (MoU), signed 2026-06-17, expired with no permanent deal. Trump said it was not a hard deadline. Araghchi said Iran had not decided to restart talks, and Qatar and Pakistan are still passing messages between the sides. [NewsNation](https://www.newsnationnow.com/world/us-iran-war-memorandum-of-understanding/), [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/8/17/us-iran-memorandum-of-understanding-expires-how-and-why-it-fell-apart)
- 2026-08-17: Iran signalled a more offensive posture. Its commanders say they have plans to defend southern islands, including Kharg, against a possible US seizure. Iran's army chief offered a bounty on US soldiers in any ground operation, and Mohsen Rezaee said the US had held off on ground plans he called "half-baked". Trump's remark that Hormuz would become US territory was later described by the White House as a joke. [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/8/17/iran-signals-readiness-for-us-ground-operations-as-mou-expires)
- 2026-07-16 to 07-17: The WSJ and Washington Post reported three options under review: more airstrikes, bombing underground nuclear sites, and sending troops to take islands near Hormuz, with Kharg named most often. The plans reportedly involve limited raids, not a full invasion. Press secretary Leavitt said "the president has not made a decision", and Rubio reportedly said the US was "not currently postured" for ground operations. [Gulf News](https://gulfnews.com/world/americas/ground-war-next-us-readies-iran-options-as-troops-move-what-we-know-1.500489863), [Fox News](https://www.foxnews.com/world/iran-responds-reports-us-weighing-ground-operations-we-never-accept-humiliation.amp), [WSWS](https://www.wsws.org/en/articles/2026/07/17/vdtb-j17.html)
- 2026-07-07 to 07-14: The ceasefire collapsed over shipping. The US reimposed its naval blockade on 07-14, and both sides traded attacks. [ABC News](https://abcnews.com/Politics/us-iran-ceasefire-mou-broke-timeline/story?id=134622392), [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/8/17/us-iran-memorandum-of-understanding-expires-how-and-why-it-fell-apart)
- 2026-03-30: Elements of the 82nd Airborne (about 1,000 troops) and about 5,000 Marines deployed to the region, with no ground entry announced. [Military.com](https://www.military.com/benefits/2026/03/30/us-ground-forces-arrive-middle-east-iran-conflict-escalates.html), [Gulf News](https://gulfnews.com/world/mena/us-marines-deploy-as-trump-weighs-seizing-iran-s-crown-jewel-kharg-island-1.500476384)

## 4. Base rates
- The war has run for about 5.5 months (roughly March to mid-August 2026). Seizing islands, especially Kharg, has been publicly discussed since March, but no non-rescue ground operation has been reported. That is 0 of about 5 months, even during the most intense phases.
- The only ground entry (April) was a rescue, which this question excludes.
- Analysts generally describe island seizures as high-risk with a low payoff because Iranian missiles and drones could hit troops holding the islands. [USNI Proceedings](https://www.usni.org/magazines/proceedings/2026/april/seizing-iranian-offshore-islands-high-risk-low-payoff), [Quincy Institute](https://quincyinst.org/research/limited-us-ground-operations-in-iran-will-not-shift-the-wars-balance/)
- Historically, the US has rarely put ground forces into Iran: the 1980 Eagle Claw rescue attempt and the 2026 rescue mission.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Manifold has a market on this exact question, which showed 14% YES in a search snippet. I could not see the date of that price or load the page. [Manifold](https://manifold.markets/CommanderKeen/will-the-us-put-boots-on-the-ground-8h8ynzZENP)
- Polymarket's "US forces enter Iran by…?" market hit 86 to 90% around 2026-04-06 and appears to have resolved YES because of the rescue. Its rules differ from this question's. [Polymarket](https://polymarket.com/event/us-forces-enter-iran-by)
- In a separate Polymarket market on a US "invasion" or control of Iranian territory by 2026-12-31, the odds peaked at 68% on 2026-03-29 and fell to 14 to 28% by mid-June. [Crypto Briefing](https://cryptobriefing.com/polymarket-us-iran-invasion-odds-2027/)
- I found no current Polymarket or Kalshi price for an August 31 deadline.

## 6. Upcoming events before September 1
- How the US follows through on the "economic operation" announced 2026-08-19, and whether military escalation comes with it.
- Whether indirect talks through Qatar and Pakistan resume, or Iran carries out its threatened offensive shift after the MoU expiry.
- Any Iranian attacks on shipping or Gulf states that could prompt US raids on Hormuz islands (Larak, Abu Musa, the Tunbs) or on Kharg.
- Any new downed-aircrew rescue would not count under the exclusion.
- Only about 12 days remain in the window.
